Potelych Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lviv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Potelych's Jewish community, present from 1487, produced two notable religious figures: the 17th-century rabbi David Segal — known as the Turei Zahav, one of the most influential commentators in Jewish law — and Menachem Mendl Landman, founder of a Hasidic dynasty that his son Itzhak inherited in 1917. The community numbered around 400 by 1931, but was killed in the Rava-Ruska ghetto in late September 1942. The cemetery, marked on maps from the 1880s through 1939, is presumed to have been demolished after the war, though it was never built over.
